title: Pranks with Louis and the band on the road
summary: Foster says he and Louis played practical jokes, such as swapping beds and the rope-and-chair trick on Paul Barbarin in Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: One can. You were just too greedy, I guess.
I always do some funny things.
I did, Louie. Was Louie pretty much of a cut up? In those days?

Yeah, Louie doing some funny things, no man. Oh Louie just too crazy. Louie doing some crazy things. And I always get into things, I used to do, aren't you see I'm a trumpet player? I used to be watching some terrible things. Write signs, steal his shoes and hats, you wear a suit, you wear a pair of shoes too long, steal them. You wear a cap too long, I'd steal them. Then I always get put, that always would be me. Like we go in a place and the guy gets a better room and I go out and buy it. We was in Mobile, Alabama. The guy had a nice room and I couldn't get over there, so I went and bought me a, about, you go get ten cents wood, you know, for the stove. You get about six or eight sticks of wood, what's so big? So I slipped in this guy's house, man, in this room, and he had this wood in a basket. And put the sheet back. Can we get some coffee? Sure.

Put the sheet back and put that wood, this is nice, in his bed, man. Put the bed. So when he come in he's going to drop right in the bed. So I went right across the street where I could peep, man. He fell in that bed, like in the back.

Then he come looking for me. Ain't nobody been here, I got to slip all around, went all around, got over some fences, they get in the back house, man, because of the shoppers that I was going to steal. People leave the back door for now, you know. But he still believes it was me. But I, but he never did find out it was me. And Paul Barberin one night, he had a chick, man, in Philadelphia. I went and bought it with some rope. And like my room is over there, when you look in this window, I run the rope all through there, on the chair. The little ropes at Douglas Hotel. He's up there toss the sheet on his bed. Oh, that's what I'm talking about? Yeah. Every once in a while, the chick would see the chair moving, you know. She's, ooh. Don't worry, babe, you were the man. Ain't scared of nothing.
